children: Finance Ministry has clarified that all the due processes were followed in strategic restructuring of IDBI Bank. It has said that government and Life Insurance Corporation will be further benefitted for their residual stake in the bank.

On October 14, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd. Under the process, the winning bid was ₹81 per share. The government is offloading 30.48 per cent of its stake and expected to get over ₹26500 crore, while LIC to sell 30.24 per cent and likely to get over ₹26,300 crore. The deal is expected to be completed by the end of the fiscal year.

After the completion of the deal, the government will have residual shareholding of 15 per cent and the LIC will have 19 per cent. Neither the government nor the LIC will have seat on the board of IDBI Bank. Also, they will not have any contingent liability. LIC will have to dilute 4 per cent stake in IDBI bank within two years to retain ownership of LIC Housing Finance.

“The GoI and the LIC retain residual shareholdings to get further benefit from the upside that is expected from the value enhancement following strategic restructuring of the IDBI Bank going forward in future,” a Finance Ministry statement issued late on Thursday said.

Number of questions have been raised on the valuation, especially keeping in mind land packets, the bank has. Meanwhile, the ministry has said that the entire valuation methodology was reviewed by the CGD (Core Group of Secretaries on Disinvestment) in April 2026 before the invitation of best offer bids. Since the comparator used for valuation has to be contemporaneous with the bids received, and March 31. 2026 closing financial accounts were released in the public domain in end-April, the independent valuation agencies had started working on the revised valuations in May 2026 itself.

“The process remained double blind because the bidder did not know the valuation and the valuators did not see the bids. It is only the CGD which gets to see a complete picture and compares the bids with fair valuations to take a final call on the reasonableness of the bids submitted,” the Ministry said.

Further, the valuation was carried out by two different advisers, independent of each other, using independent and distinct methodologies. Also, since suitable comparable transaction were not available, comparable companies’ method was used, which in this case were all the listed public sector banks.  The Asset Valuer also used robust and time-tested methodologies, including additional value for disputed tax demands, which were indemnified as a common demand of the qualified bidders to nudge the bid offer upwards.

“This remains a low probability event and revenue neutral for the government, as only the additional tax demand, if paid at all, will be eligible for reimbursement. The potential liability that could arise on this account was only ₹627 crores while the bid discovered price increased by ₹3,917 crores enhancing the value of the transaction for the GoI and the LIC,” the Ministry said.

title: Govt, LIC to get benefit from residual stake in IDBI Bank upside
